The Bloom filters were built so that the false-positive rate is at most **1/10⁸** (one in 100 million) (p. 8, Section 4 "Generalization vs Memorization").

The text layer prints this as "1018", which looks like 10¹⁸. The PDF page shows it's actually the fraction 1 over 10⁸, flattened when the text was extracted (p. 8).

Context from the same passage (p. 8):
- The filters held the 8-grams of the WebText training set. Strings were first normalized to lower-case alphanumeric words separated by single spaces, to improve recall.
- The authors checked the low false-positive rate by generating 1M strings. The filter matched none of them.
- They used the filters to measure what share of each test set's 8-grams also appear in WebText training (Table 6, p. 8).
